en.commentary:
I ranked electric blankets by one question first: if this thing stays plugged in next to me for eight hours tonight, what evidence do I have that it will behave? That question reorders the whole category, because this year's safety problems came from the cheapest and easiest blankets to buy.

At the end of July 2026 the CPSC announced a recall of about 178,000 OCTROT heated sherpa throws and blankets sold on Amazon between August 2021 and December 2025 for $40 to $60. The cord can detach and ignite, and the agency counted 555 reports of melting, sparking or smoking, including 27 fires and 15 injuries. On July 16 the CPSC told owners of roughly 700 Melinora blankets to stop using them after heating wires melted through the fabric, and it issued that notice as a warning because the manufacturer, Leevana Inc., stopped responding to the agency. Both products were low-priced, sold through Amazon and carried names nobody would recognize in a store.

So my top three are brands with a named safety listing, a five-year warranty and a clean record in the CPSC electric blanket recalls I checked from 2016 through 2026. Beautyrest wins on control: 20 heat settings between 85 and 105°F, a timer you choose from 1 to 10 hours, two controllers on a queen, UL certification and OEKO-TEX fabric. Pure Enrichment is the easiest recommendation on price at $99.99 in every size on its own store. Serta comes third, and here is the detail most shoppers never see: Beautyrest and Serta heated blankets are both made by the same licensee, JLA Home, so the choice between them comes down to the controller and the price tag.

Two well-known brands carry recall history. Sunbeam recalled 43,000 queen blankets in March 2023, and Bedsure recalled about 350,000 heating blankets and pads the same month. Both recalls covered specific model numbers and sale windows. I still like Sunbeam's Royal Ultra at about $60, so I scored the record honestly and let price and controls carry it to fifth.

Running cost is the quiet argument for the whole category. A queen blanket drawing 200 W for eight hours uses 1.6 kWh, about 29 cents at the 18.02-cent average residential rate the EIA projects for 2026. A 1,500 W space heater over the same eight hours costs about $2.16. That gap is why I warm the bed and let the room stay cool.

Three models here come from the Taiwan market, and all three are under-blankets you lie on. Beurer's TP 88 XXL and Northern's NR-361G both print their BSMI inspection numbers on the product page, and that printed number is the check I weight most for Taiwan buyers. When Taiwan's Consumer Protection Committee and BSMI bought 10 electric blankets from online and retail channels in 2021, three failed, with results announced in March 2022.

highlights.title: Check the seller's recall record before you touch the fabric
highlights.body: The CPSC database is the most useful spec sheet in this category. OCTROT's 178,000-unit recall followed 555 incident reports, and Melinora's warning came after five reports and one burn injury from a manufacturer that went silent. Among the brands I ranked, Beautyrest, Pure Enrichment, Serta and Degrees of Comfort have a clean record in the 2016 to 2026 electric blanket recalls I reviewed. Sunbeam (43,000 queens, March 2023) and Bedsure (about 350,000 blankets and pads, March 2023) each have one, and I scored that column down for both. Search the brand name on cpsc.gov before you buy. It takes one minute.

highlights.title: Beautyrest earns first place with the finest control on the list
highlights.body: Twenty heat settings across an 85 to 105°F window is the widest usable adjustment I found, and the timer runs anywhere from 1 to 10 hours so you can match it to the time you actually fall asleep. A queen ships with two controllers, the blanket carries UL and OEKO-TEX certification, and the warranty runs five years. Queen pricing moves between about $104 and $152 depending on the retailer, which is the one column where Pure Enrichment's flat $99.99 comes out ahead.

highlights.title: Beautyrest and Serta share a maker, so choose on the controller
highlights.body: Both brands license their heated bedding to JLA Home, which manufactures the blankets and handles warranty claims for each. That makes the decision simple. Pick Beautyrest for 20 settings and a UL listing. Pick Serta for the longer 1 to 12 hour timer and an ETL listing at $115 to $141 for a queen. Both use dual controllers on queen and larger sizes, so couples get independent sides with either one.

highlights.title: A warm bed costs about 29 cents a night
highlights.body: Pure Enrichment publishes 200 W for its queen and king blankets. Eight hours at full power is 1.6 kWh, and at the EIA's projected 2026 average residential rate of 18.02 cents that works out to about 29 cents. Blanket thermostats cycle, so real nights land lower. A 1,500 W space heater over the same eight hours uses 12 kWh and costs about $2.16. For keeping one bed warm, the blanket does the job on roughly one seventh of the electricity.

highlights.title: A 3-hour shut-off makes it a couch blanket
highlights.body: Auto shut-off length tells you what a product was designed for. Bedsure's GentleSoft throw stops after 3 hours, which suits an evening on the sofa. Sunbeam's Royal Ultra queen and Serta run up to 12 hours, Beautyrest up to 10, and Pure Enrichment a fixed 10. For overnight bedding I want at least 8 hours, and four of my top five meet that. Beurer's TP 88 XXL stops at 6 hours, and I accept that trade for its 60 W per side and its printed BSMI number.

zh-tw.commentary:
先講結論，電熱毯這個品類我第一個看安全紀錄，布料軟硬排在很後面。理由很簡單，這東西整晚插著電蓋在你身上，今年美國出事的偏偏就是最便宜、最好買的那一群。

2026 年 7 月底，美國消費品安全委員會 CPSC 公告 OCTROT 在 Amazon 賣的雪花絨電熱毯召回，數量大約 17.8 萬件，2021 年 8 月到 2025 年 12 月之間賣出，售價 40 到 60 美元。問題出在電源線會脫落起火，累計 555 起熔化、冒火花或冒煙的通報，其中 27 起火災、15 人受傷。7 月 16 日 CPSC 又對大約 700 件 Melinora 電熱毯發出停用警告，發熱線會過熱熔穿布料，製造商 Leevana 對 CPSC 完全沒有回應，只好由官方直接發警告。兩件事的共通點講白了就是三個：便宜、Amazon 第三方賣家、叫不出名字的品牌。

所以我前三名給了有安全認證、有五年保固，而且在我查的 2016 到 2026 年 CPSC 電熱毯召回清單裡找不到的品牌。Beautyrest 第一，20 段溫控落在華氏 85 到 105 度，定時 1 到 10 小時自己選，雙人尺寸附兩個控制器，UL 認證加 OEKO-TEX 布料。Pure Enrichment 第二，官網全尺寸一律 99.99 美元，換算大約 NT$3,150。Serta 第三，這裡要跟大家說一件很少人知道的事，Beautyrest 跟 Serta 的電熱毯其實是同一家授權廠 JLA Home 做的，兩個要挑哪個，看控制器跟價格就好。

有召回紀錄的知名品牌也有兩家。Sunbeam 在 2023 年 3 月召回 4.3 萬條雙人電熱毯，Bedsure 同一個月召回約 35 萬件電熱毯與電熱墊。兩次都只涉及特定型號與銷售期間，Sunbeam Royal Ultra 大約 60 美元的價格我還是很喜歡，所以這一欄照實扣分，其他交給價格跟功能去拚，最後落在第五。

說到電費，這是整個品類最有說服力的地方。美國雙人電熱毯 200 瓦開 8 小時是 1.6 度電，1,500 瓦電暖器開同樣時間是 12 度，差了七倍多。

最後是台灣讀者最該看的部分。這份榜單有三款是台灣通路買得到的，德國博依 TP 88 XXL、北方 NR-361G 跟三樂事 SP2701，前兩款都把商檢字號直接印在商品頁上。台灣的電熱毯大多是鋪在床墊上、人躺在上面的床墊型，美國主流則是蓋在身上的蓋毯型，用起來差很多。換算台灣電價，北方 120 瓦開 8 小時不到 1 度電，照非夏月每度 1.78 元算，一晚大約 NT$1.7，比超商一顆茶葉蛋還便宜。

highlights.title: 買電熱毯先查召回紀錄，這一步只要一分鐘
highlights.body: CPSC 的召回資料庫是這個品類最好用的規格表。OCTROT 17.8 萬件召回之前累積了 555 起通報，Melinora 則是 5 起通報、1 人燙傷，製造商還直接已讀不回。我排進榜單的品牌裡，Beautyrest、Pure Enrichment、Serta 跟 Degrees of Comfort 在 2016 到 2026 年的電熱毯召回清單裡都找不到，Sunbeam（2023 年 3 月，4.3 萬條雙人毯）跟 Bedsure（2023 年 3 月，約 35 萬件）各有一次，這一欄我兩家都扣分。買美國品牌之前上 cpsc.gov 搜一下品牌名，一分鐘就查完。

highlights.title: 在台灣買，商檢字號印在頁面上的直接加分
highlights.body: 電熱毯在台灣屬於應施檢驗商品，沒通過檢驗就不能上架。可是市面上還是有漏網之魚，行政院消保處跟標準檢驗局 2021 年從網購平台等通路買了 10 件電熱毯送驗，2022 年 3 月公布結果，3 件不合格，1 件標示不符、1 件品質不合格而且涉及逃避檢驗、1 件品質不合格。德國博依 TP 88 XXL 的字號 T36153、北方 NR-361G 的 T33246 都直接寫在商品頁，這種我最放心。三樂事 SP2701 的商品頁我沒看到字號，下單前記得看包裝上的商品檢驗標識。至於代購進來的美國電熱毯，身上沒有台灣的商品檢驗標識，保固也得找美國原廠處理，這點要先想清楚。

highlights.title: Beautyrest 跟 Serta 同一家廠做的，挑控制器就好
highlights.body: 兩個牌子的電熱寢具都授權給 JLA Home 生產，保固申請也是 JLA Home 在處理。所以決策很簡單，想要 20 段溫控跟 UL 認證就選 Beautyrest，想要 1 到 12 小時的長定時跟 ETL 認證就選 Serta，雙人款 115 到 141 美元，換算大約 NT$3,600 到 4,400。兩家雙人以上都是雙控制器，怕熱的跟怕冷的睡同一張床也能各自調。

highlights.title: 電熱毯一晚的電費，比一顆茶葉蛋還便宜
highlights.body: 德國博依 TP 88 XXL 每邊 60 瓦，兩邊全開 120 瓦，睡滿 6 小時自動斷電是 0.72 度。北方 NR-361G 120 瓦開 8 小時是 0.96 度，照台電非夏月每度 1.78 元算，一晚大約 NT$1.7，而且溫控器會自己跳，實際更少。對照一台 1,200 瓦的電暖器開 8 小時是 9.6 度，一個月天天開就是 288 度，光這台就會把你家電費推進更高的級距。寒流來的晚上想睡得暖，暖被窩比暖整個房間划算太多。

highlights.title: 台灣濕冷的冬天，我選床墊型
highlights.body: 台灣買得到的電熱毯大多是床墊型，鋪在床墊上、人躺在上面，上面再蓋自己的棉被，熱從下面上來、被子把熱關住，寒流天的濕冷感消得很快。德國博依 TP 88 XXL 就是這種設計，雙人雙控、每邊 60 瓦、6 小時自動斷電，睡前開、半夜自己關，電源線拆掉整條可以機洗，保固三年，官方購物網 NT$4,780，大概是一台入門除濕機的價錢。預算想壓在三千以內，北方 NR-361G 的 NT$2,980 一樣有字號、一樣是雙人尺寸，保固一年。

en.commentary:
My ranking holds this week, and the Beautyrest Plush Heated Blanket keeps first place at 9.1. It is a machine-washable microlight plush blanket with a digital controller, multiple heat settings and an automatic shut-off, and it wins because its controller gives the finest heat steps on this list from a brand with a clean recent recall record.

No new heated blanket recall has been posted in the past week. The July OCTROT recall is still circulating, and WRAL's coverage keeps the numbers in front of shoppers: more than 170,000 sherpa throws sold on Amazon, 555 reports of melting, sparking or smoking, 27 fires and 15 injuries. If you bought a cheap sherpa heated throw online in the last few years, check the brand name against the CPSC notice before the first cold night.

Mid-September is the right moment for what I call the first-night inspection. Before you plug in a blanket that spent the summer folded in a closet, lay it flat and run your hand along the whole surface for hard spots or kinks in the wiring. Check the cord where it meets the connector for cracks or discoloration. Then run it on low for fifteen minutes while you stay in the room. A blanket that develops a hot spot gets retired, with no second chances.

Pure Enrichment PureRelief Deluxe holds second at 8.9 for its fast warm-up, and the Beurer TP 88 XXL stays fourth at 8.5 as the under-blanket I recommend for Taiwan buyers. It carries local support, a timer and a double-bed size that heats the mattress before you get in.

Taiwan's standards bureau has tested electric blankets on the local market, and I still treat that report as required reading for anyone shopping from marketplaces this winter.

en.commentary: Beautyrest's Plush Heated Blanket keeps the top spot on the same 9.5 recall record and strong certification scores that have anchored this ranking's safety focus for weeks, and this fall has made that focus look more justified than ever. The CPSC recalled roughly 195,000 JKMAX heated blankets and pads in September after 577 reports of smoking, melting, or burning that caused 53 burn injuries, and that recall landed just two months after a separate July recall pulled more than 170,000 Octrot electric throws over cords that could detach and ignite, with 27 fires tied to that one alone. Neither brand appears anywhere in this ranking, and that's the point: every competitor on this list cleared the certification and recall-history bar that both of those products failed. Beautyrest's 8.8 washability score reflects a controller that detaches cleanly for machine washing on a gentle cycle, the method that actually protects the internal wiring, the exact failure point behind both of this fall's recalls. Pure Enrichment's PureRelief Deluxe holds second on a matching 9.5 recall record and a slightly higher 8.8 cost-per-night score, a real option for anyone prioritizing lower electricity cost. Serta's own Plush Heated Blanket holds third on a 9.5 recall record paired with a 9.5 auto shut-off score, the highest shut-off number in this entire list. I'm holding every rank steady today. Two serious recalls inside three months is exactly the kind of year that rewards sticking with brands that already have a clean safety record.

Pure Enrichment stays second on the strongest value score in the top tier at 8.6, a $99.99 flat price across every size that undercuts Beautyrest without giving up safety certification. The marketplace-only brands at the bottom, Bedsure especially with a 5.0 recall-record score, are exactly the kind of listing this week's new recall should make you think twice about.
